hostname.description: Server hostname shown in the config file header comment

log_dir.description: Base directory where all log files are written

include_kern_log.description: Write all kernel facility messages to kern.log

include_mail_log.description: Write all mail facility messages to mail.log (async write)

include_daemon_log.description: Write all daemon facility messages to daemon.log (async write)

include_cron_log.description: Write all cron/at facility messages to cron.log

include_syslog_log.description: Write syslogd's own internal messages to syslog

include_messages.description: Write catch-all info+ messages (excluding mail, auth, cron) to messages

debug_log_enabled.description: Enable a separate debug-level log file — very high volume, off by default in production

emergency_wall.description: Broadcast *.emerg messages to all logged-in users' terminals via wall

remote_logging_enabled.description: Forward all log messages to a remote syslog server

remote_host.description: Hostname or IP address of the remote syslog receiver

remote_port.description: Port of the remote syslog receiver (standard syslog port: 514)

remote_protocol.description: Transport for remote forwarding: 'udp' (single @ prefix, low overhead) or 'tcp' (@@ prefix, reliable — verify daemon support)

extra_rules.description: Additional custom syslog rules appended after the standard ruleset

selector.description: Syslog facility.severity selector expression, e.g. 'local0.*' or '*.warn;cron.none'

action.description: Log destination: file path (optionally - prefixed for async), @host (UDP remote), @@host (TCP remote), * (wall all users), or |/path/to/pipe

comment.description: One-line human-readable description rendered as a # comment above this rule
